headline: Lawson is disqualified from Mexico qualifying and starts from the back
body: Lawson had qualified eighth for Racing Bulls, ninth after his one-place penalty for the FP2 collision with Verstappen. The stewards disqualified him for not reducing MGU-K deployment at the required rate after his fastest Q2 lap, and he starts the race from the back of the grid.

headline: Stewards set lap-one rules for Turns 1 to 6 in Mexico
body: On lap one and the first lap after any restart, cars are treated as both attacking and defending through Turns 1 to 3 and Turns 4 to 6. A car that leaves the track and stays ahead of a car close behind may be judged to have gained a lasting advantage unless it yields the position by Turn 4, or by Turn 12 for the second section.

headline: Hadjar gets a formal warning for pushing a paddock visitor
body: The stewards found Hadjar breached the regulations when he pushed aside a guest in the paddock before FP1. No further penalty was given, with the stewards citing provocation, congestion and a lack of security.
